templates.name: Explain (cause, origin, advantage, mechanism, definition, significance)
Present or describe to an already familiar audience
Introduce or describe to an unfamiliar or new audience
Specify or identify a single fact

items.subtype: Explain how a method works (tracing a honey’s origin)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Honeybees make honey from flower nectar, and the honey typically contains pollen from the flowers they visit.
• Each plant species produces pollen grains with a distinctive size, shape, and surface texture.
• In melissopalynology, analysts examine a honey sample under a microscope, identifying its pollen grains and calculating the proportion of each type.
• The plant species growing in an area vary considerably from one geographic region to another.
• Honeys advertised as originating in a particular place frequently command premium prices.
items.stem: The student wants to explain how melissopalynology can reveal where a honey was produced. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Honeys advertised as coming from a particular place often command premium prices, so analysts examine the pollen in them.
Since pollen grains from a single plant species vary in size and shape depending on the region where the plant grows, measuring the pollen in a honey shows where it was made.
Identifying the pollen in a honey reveals which plants the bees visited, and since different regions support different mixes of plants, that pollen points to the honey’s source.
Under a microscope, analysts can recognize the pollen grains in a honey sample, since each plant species produces pollen of a distinctive size, shape, and texture.
items.explanation: The goal is to explain how the method reveals where a honey came from. The pollen in a honey comes from the flowers the bees used, and the plants that grow in an area vary by region. Choice C links these two facts: identifying the pollen shows which plants were visited, and the plants point to the region.

A.recipe: OG (a motive for the analysis, not how it works)
A.why_wrong: It gives a reason someone might want to check a honey’s origin, not how the analysis reveals that origin.

B.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: variation moved from the mix of species to the grains themselves)
B.why_wrong: The notes say each species has distinctive pollen and that regions differ in which species grow there; they never say one species’ pollen changes from region to region.

D.why_wrong: It explains how analysts identify the pollen but never connects the pollen to the plants of a region, so it does not explain how the honey’s origin is revealed.

items.notes: Subject: science (food science, palynology). No named people. Band 6: PART, FALSE, OG as in d4b07ce6 (PART, FALSE, PART). Key joins bullets 1, 3 and 4 through a link no bullet states (pollen identifies the plants visited; the regional plant mix identifies the place). B is goal-shaped: it explains a mechanism but misplaces the variation. No bullet states the conclusion.

fixes: rewrote bullet 1: in "pollen from the flowers they visit frequently ends up in it," the adverb could attach to "visit" or to "ends up"

band7.why: Planned band 6. Key links three bullets through a step no bullet states (pollen identifies plants, the regional plant mix identifies the place) in its own words; B is a goal-shaped FALSE mechanism, D a first-step PART, A off-goal. One FALSE distractor, so short of the band-7 gate.

items.subtype: Contrast on an evaluative dimension (drawbacks)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Solar cookers use sunlight, rather than fuel, to prepare food.
• A box cooker is an insulated box with a transparent lid that traps heat.
• Once positioned, it can operate unattended for hours, but cooking takes twice as long as on a stove.
• A parabolic cooker uses a curved reflector to concentrate sunlight onto a pot.
• It cooks as quickly as a conventional stove but must be repositioned every 15 to 30 minutes to remain aligned with the Sun.
items.stem: The student wants to contrast the drawbacks of the two kinds of solar cookers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: A box cooker traps heat under a transparent lid, whereas a parabolic cooker concentrates sunlight with a curved reflector.
A box cooker cooks more slowly than a parabolic cooker does, but the parabolic cooker needs far more tending to stay aimed at the Sun.
Both kinds of solar cookers take longer than a stove to prepare food, and a parabolic cooker must also be repositioned every 15 to 30 minutes.
Unlike a parabolic cooker, which must be repositioned every 15 to 30 minutes, a box cooker can operate unattended for hours.
items.explanation: The goal is to contrast the cookers’ drawbacks. According to the notes, a box cooker takes twice as long as a stove, while a parabolic cooker cooks as quickly as one, so the box cooker is the slower of the two. A parabolic cooker must be repositioned every 15 to 30 minutes, while a box cooker can run unattended for hours, so the parabolic cooker needs more tending. Choice B sets these two drawbacks side by side.

A.recipe: REL (true contrast on the wrong dimension: how each cooker works)
A.why_wrong: It contrasts how the two cookers capture the Sun’s heat, not their drawbacks.

C.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: gives the box cooker’s slowness to both)
C.why_wrong: The notes say a parabolic cooker cooks as quickly as a conventional stove; only the box cooker is slower.

D.recipe: PART (one drawback set against the other cooker’s advantage)
D.why_wrong: It gives the parabolic cooker’s drawback but sets it against an advantage of the box cooker, so the box cooker’s drawback, slow cooking, is missing.

items.notes: Subject: technology and society (solar cooking). General knowledge; no named people or figures beyond rough cooking times. Band 6 as in e98b1690 and de01ccef: the compared dimension is evaluative (drawbacks), each cooker carries one advantage and one drawback, so D (drawback against advantage) and C (a false shared drawback) are both close. Temperatures left out so no option offers a second, arguable drawback.

fixes: rewrote key B: it named "drawback" twice (the only option carrying the goal word) and copied bullet wording; it now states both drawbacks as derived comparisons (slower; needs far more tending), as in e98b1690; explanation updated

band7.why: Evaluative DIFF as in e98b1690: key now states both drawbacks as derived comparisons without naming them; C is a goal-shaped FALSE shared drawback, D sets a drawback against an advantage, A contrasts on the wrong dimension. One FALSE distractor, so band 6.

items.subtype: Present a study’s findings to an audience familiar with a concept
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ecosystem engineers are organisms that create or modify habitats in ways that affect other species.
• Aardvarks dig extensive burrows in the grasslands of southern Africa.
• A team of researchers installed motion-activated cameras at aardvark burrows in South Africa.
• Over two years, cameras recorded 27 other species of mammals and birds using the burrows, frequently during the hottest hours.
• The researchers’ sensors showed burrow temperatures fluctuating by only a few degrees, while outside temperatures varied by more than 20°C daily.
items.stem: The student wants to present the study’s findings to an audience already familiar with ecosystem engineers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Aardvarks are ecosystem engineers, organisms that modify habitats in ways that affect other species, and the study found that their burrows sheltered 27 other species from the heat.
Ecosystem engineers create or modify habitats in ways that affect other species, as aardvarks do when they dig burrows in the grasslands of southern Africa.
A team of researchers installed motion-activated cameras at aardvark burrows in South Africa and left them running for two years.
The study showed aardvarks acting as ecosystem engineers: their burrows held a nearly steady temperature and were used by 27 other species, often to escape the heat.
items.explanation: An audience already familiar with ecosystem engineers does not need the term explained. Choice D uses the term without defining it and presents what the study found: the burrows stayed at a nearly steady temperature and were used by 27 other species, often during the hottest hours.

A.recipe: AUD (complete findings, but redefines the familiar term)
A.why_wrong: It presents the findings but stops to define ecosystem engineers, which this audience already knows.

B.recipe: AUD + PART (definition and background, no findings)
B.why_wrong: It defines ecosystem engineers and says aardvarks dig burrows but reports nothing the study found.

C.why_wrong: It describes how the study was done, not what it found.

items.notes: Subject: science (ecology). Team left unnamed; figures illustrative (no fact-checking for this skill). Plan cell asked band 7, but AUD_FAM has no band-7 official items (spec/rw/band7/rhetorical_synthesis.md), so written as strong band 6 per WAVE.md. Distractors AUD, AUD + PART, PART as in 39ccb463 (AUD, AUD, PART); A is the 2.1 D pattern (complete, fails only by redefining). Key paraphrases bullets 4 and 5 (nearly steady temperature, escape the heat).

fixes: bullet 5 now credits the burrow temperatures to the team (the key says "the study showed" a steady temperature, which the notes did not tie to the study); trimmed bullet 2
option C stated an aim the notes never give ("To learn which animals visit"); it now gives only the method from bullets 3 and 4

band7.why: AUD_FAM has no band-7 official items, so it cannot be band 7; a strong band 6 as in 39ccb463: A has the full findings but redefines the term, B defines with no findings, C gives the method.

items.subtype: Describe a process (a pump’s cycle)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A hydraulic ram is a pump that harnesses the momentum of flowing water, without electricity, to lift some of that water uphill.
• Water descends through a drive pipe and initially escapes through an open waste valve.
• As the water accelerates, its momentum forces the waste valve shut, abruptly halting the flow.
• The resulting pressure surge drives a little water through a one-way valve into an air chamber, compressing the trapped air.
• The compressed air subsequently propels that water through a delivery pipe, and the waste valve reopens automatically.
items.stem: The student wants to describe how a hydraulic ram lifts water uphill. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In a hydraulic ram, rushing water slams the waste valve shut so suddenly that the jolt of pressure pushes some of it into an air chamber, where squeezed air sends it uphill.
In a hydraulic ram, compressed air from an air chamber forces the waste valve shut, and the resulting surge pushes the water in the drive pipe up a delivery pipe.
In a hydraulic ram, speeding water forces the one-way valve shut, and the resulting surge sends water out through the waste valve to an air chamber that pushes it up the delivery pipe.
In a hydraulic ram, water first collects in an air chamber; once the air inside is compressed, the waste valve snaps shut, sending a surge of water up the delivery pipe.
items.explanation: The notes describe a sequence: water accelerating down the drive pipe forces the waste valve shut, the sudden stop creates a pressure surge that forces some water into an air chamber, and the compressed air pushes that water up the delivery pipe. Choice A describes these steps in the right order and with the right causes.

B.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: wrong agent closes the valve)
B.why_wrong: According to the notes, the momentum of the flowing water forces the waste valve shut; the compressed air comes into play only after water has been driven into the chamber.

C.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: the two valves’ roles swapped)
C.why_wrong: It swaps the valves. According to the notes, the water’s momentum forces the waste valve shut, and the surge then drives water through the one-way valve into the air chamber.

D.recipe: FALSE (goal-shaped: steps in the wrong order)
D.why_wrong: The water enters the air chamber after the waste valve has shut, pushed by the surge of pressure; it does not collect there first.

items.notes: Subject: technology (water pumping). Standard mechanism, no named people. Band 7 recipe from b07a7634 (FALSE, FALSE, FALSE). Section 6 checks: 3 FALSE, all goal-shaped; note register 5.21 chars per word (passes the 5.2 line), 12.8% long words (below the 14% line); a goal-only read leaves all four options describing a process; derived wording in the key (jolt of pressure, squeezed air). Different mechanism from the w2b3 tide mill (no storing and releasing a tide).
band7_moves: an ordered process over four bullets with distinct agents (water, waste valve, one-way valve, air chamber), as in b07a7634, written as plain bullets without step labels
three goal-shaped FALSE options, each describing a full cycle but misplacing one agent or step (air closes the valve; surge while the valve is open; chamber fills before the valve shuts)
the key compresses four bullets and states the cause (the sudden stop produces the pressure) in words no bullet uses

fixes: key named "a valve" though the notes have two; now "the waste valve"
replaced distractor C (killed by the word "open" in bullet 2) with a goal-shaped valve swap that needs the two valves traced, as in b07a7634

band7.why: Meets the DESC recipe of b07a7634: three goal-shaped FALSE distractors (wrong agent shuts the valve, valves swapped, steps out of order), each found only by tracing the bullets; key in its own words (slams, jolt, squeezed air); notes at 5.21 characters per word (section 6 check 1). Passage kept at 104 words so the hard tier stays at CB register; section 6 checks 1, 3 and 5 pass.

items.subtype: Difference with no attribute named (comparative adjective)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Each annual growth ring in a tree trunk consists of two layers: earlywood and latewood.
• Earlywood forms in spring, when the tree is growing rapidly.
• Its cells are relatively large, with thin walls, giving the layer a pale appearance.
• Latewood forms later in the growing season, as growth gradually slows.
• Its cells are comparatively small, with thick walls, giving the layer a dark appearance.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between earlywood and latewood. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Earlywood and latewood are the two layers that make up each annual growth ring in a tree trunk.
Earlywood, which forms in spring when a tree is growing rapidly, consists of relatively large cells with thin walls.
Earlywood and latewood, the two layers of each annual growth ring, differ from each other in several ways.
Latewood, which forms as a tree’s growth slows, is darker than earlywood because its cells are smaller and thicker walled.
items.explanation: Choice D compares the two layers directly: latewood is darker than earlywood because its cells are smaller and thicker walled. That emphasizes a difference between them.

A.why_wrong: It says what earlywood and latewood have in common, not how they differ.

B.why_wrong: It describes earlywood but says nothing about latewood.

C.recipe: VAGUE (states that they differ without saying how)
C.why_wrong: It claims the layers differ but never says in what way.

items.notes: Subject: science (botany). General knowledge. Goal names no attribute, as in 2.11; the notes give each layer its color once, so only the key states a difference. Frame: comparative adjective (darker than), not while/whereas.

items.subtype: Difference on a named attribute (Unlike opener)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bharatanatyam and Kathak are two of India’s major classical dance traditions.
• Bharatanatyam originated in temples in southern India.
• Its dancers perform much of each piece in a half-seated position, with their knees bent outward.
• Kathak developed in northern India and was later performed in royal courts.
• Its dancers maintain a largely upright stance with straight legs and are celebrated for rapid sequences of spins.
items.stem: The student wants to contrast the posture of dancers in the two dance forms. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Unlike Bharatanatyam dancers, who often bend their knees in a half-seated position, Kathak dancers keep their legs mostly straight.
Bharatanatyam originated in temples in southern India, while Kathak developed in northern India and was later performed in royal courts.
Kathak dancers, who maintain a largely upright stance, are celebrated for performing rapid sequences of spins.
Bharatanatyam and Kathak are both major classical dance traditions that developed in India.
items.explanation: The goal is to contrast how dancers hold their bodies. Choice A sets Bharatanatyam’s half-seated position, with bent knees, against the upright stance and straight legs of Kathak dancers.

B.recipe: REL (true contrast on the wrong attribute: origins)
B.why_wrong: It contrasts where the two forms developed, not the dancers’ posture.

C.why_wrong: It describes Kathak dancers only and says nothing about Bharatanatyam.

D.why_wrong: It states what the two forms share rather than a difference.

items.notes: Subject: arts (dance). General knowledge, no named people. Frame: Unlike opener. Distractors REL (origins), PART, REL (similarity).

fixes: trimmed bullet 2 (no option used Tamil Nadu)

items.subtype: Contrast with a concession first (what judges rely on)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The world’s legal systems largely belong to one of two traditions: civil law or common law.
• In both traditions, judges are obligated to apply legislation passed by lawmakers.
• In civil law systems, such as France’s, judges decide cases primarily by applying comprehensive written codes.
• In common law systems, such as those of the United Kingdom and the United States, judges also rely heavily on previous court decisions, known as precedents.
items.stem: The student wants to contrast what judges in the two traditions rely on to decide cases. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In both the civil law and the common law traditions, judges must apply the legislation that lawmakers pass.
The civil law tradition is followed in France, whereas the common law tradition is followed in the United Kingdom and the United States.
Although judges in both traditions apply legislation, common law judges also lean heavily on past court rulings, while civil law judges work mainly from written codes.
In common law systems, such as those of the United Kingdom and the United States, judges rely heavily on previous court decisions, which are known as precedents.
items.explanation: The goal is to contrast what judges in each tradition rely on. Choice C first notes what the traditions share and then gives the difference: common law judges lean heavily on earlier court decisions, while civil law judges mainly apply written codes.

A.why_wrong: It states only what judges in the two traditions have in common.

B.recipe: REL (true contrast on the wrong attribute: where each is used)
B.why_wrong: It contrasts where the two traditions are followed, not what judges rely on to decide cases.

D.why_wrong: It describes what common law judges rely on but says nothing about judges in civil law systems.

items.notes: Subject: social science (law). General knowledge. Frame: concession then difference (Although both ..., while ...), the 3.3 move at medium level. Distractors REL (similarity), REL (wrong attribute), PART.

items.subtype: Introduce a concept to a new audience
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A community land trust (CLT) is a nonprofit organization that owns land on behalf of a community.
• A CLT sells the houses on its land but retains ownership of the land itself.
• Because purchasers pay only for the house, these homes typically cost considerably less than comparable homes nearby.
• When owners resell, they accept a price limit so that the home remains affordable for subsequent buyers.
• The first CLT in the United States was established in Georgia in 1969.
items.stem: The student wants to introduce community land trusts to a new audience. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The first community land trust in the United States was established in Georgia in 1969.
A community land trust is a nonprofit that owns land for a community and sells the houses on it at lower prices, with resale limits that keep them affordable.
Purchasers of these homes, which cost less than comparable homes nearby, accept a price limit when they resell so that each home remains affordable.
Community land trusts sell the houses on their land but retain ownership of the land itself.
items.explanation: Introducing community land trusts to a new audience means saying what they are and what they do. Choice B explains that a community land trust is a nonprofit that owns land for a community and sells the homes on it at lower prices, with limits that keep them affordable.

A.recipe: OG (date and place of the first one)
A.why_wrong: It gives a historical fact without explaining what a community land trust is.

C.why_wrong: It refers to “these homes” and a price limit without saying what a community land trust is, so a new audience would not follow it.

D.why_wrong: It gives one feature of community land trusts but not what they are or that they keep homes affordable.

items.notes: Subject: social science (housing). General knowledge; the 1969 Georgia trust is New Communities Inc. Distractors OG, AUD, PART as in 2.26 (OG, PART, PART) and 2.43 (AUD).

items.subtype: Describe a work to an audience unfamiliar with the artist
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Saule Tolegenova is a Kazakh American artist who works primarily with felt.
• Felt, produced by pressing moistened wool fibers together, has traditionally covered the portable dwellings of nomadic peoples in Central Asia.
• Tolegenova’s installation Steppe Wind (2018) consists of 240 strips of hand-dyed felt.
• The strips are suspended from the ceiling at varying heights.
• Small electric fans positioned around the gallery keep the strips continuously swaying.
items.stem: The student wants to describe Steppe Wind to an audience unfamiliar with Saule Tolegenova. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tolegenova’s 2018 installation Steppe Wind features 240 strips of hand-dyed felt that hang from the ceiling at varying heights and are kept swaying by small fans placed around the gallery.
Saule Tolegenova, a Kazakh American artist, works primarily with felt, a material that traditionally covered the portable dwellings of Central Asian nomads.
Felt, which Tolegenova used in her 2018 installation Steppe Wind, is produced by pressing moistened wool fibers together.
Steppe Wind, a 2018 installation by Kazakh American artist Saule Tolegenova, consists of 240 strips of hand-dyed felt hanging from the ceiling and swaying in the breeze from fans.
items.explanation: For an audience that does not know Tolegenova, the sentence should say who she is while describing the work. Choice D identifies her as a Kazakh American artist and describes Steppe Wind: 240 strips of hand-dyed felt hanging from the ceiling, kept moving by fans.

A.recipe: AUD (describes the work but treats the artist as known)
A.why_wrong: It describes Steppe Wind but gives no information about who Tolegenova is.

B.recipe: OG (introduces the artist, not the work)
B.why_wrong: It introduces Tolegenova and her material but does not describe Steppe Wind.

C.why_wrong: It explains how felt is made rather than describing the installation, and it does not say who Tolegenova is.

items.notes: Subject: arts (installation). Invented artist and work: “Saule Tolegenova” searched once (2026-10-16), no real person with that name; nearest hits were the painter Saule Suleimenova and the singer Bibigul Tulegenova, different names. Distractors AUD, OG, OG as in 2.36 (AUD, OG, PART).

items.subtype: Emphasize how rare an event is
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Neelakurinji is a flowering shrub native to the high-altitude grasslands of the Western Ghats, a mountain range in southern India.
• Its name combines neela, the Malayalam word for “blue,” with kurinji, the plant’s regional name.
• The shrub blooms only once every twelve years.
• During a flowering season, its small violet-blue blossoms can carpet entire hillsides.
• The hill town of Munnar, in Kerala, attracts enormous crowds of tourists whenever the shrubs bloom.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize how rarely neelakurinji flowers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Neelakurinji, a shrub of India’s Western Ghats, blooms just once every twelve years.
When neelakurinji flowers, its small violet-blue blossoms can carpet entire hillsides in the Western Ghats.
Whenever neelakurinji blooms, the hill town of Munnar in Kerala attracts enormous crowds of tourists.
Neelakurinji, whose name includes the Malayalam word for “blue,” is native to the high-altitude grasslands of the Western Ghats.
items.explanation: Choice A emphasizes how rarely the shrub flowers by stating that it blooms just once every twelve years.

B.why_wrong: It describes what a bloom looks like, not how seldom one happens.

C.why_wrong: It reports that blooms draw crowds but does not say how often the shrub flowers.

D.why_wrong: It explains part of the plant’s name and where it grows, not how rarely it flowers.

items.notes: Subject: science (botany). Strobilanthes kunthiana, last mass bloom 2018; general knowledge. Distractors OG, OG, OG as in 2.40 and 2.33. Key is the shortest option, as in 2.33 and 2.20.

items.subtype: Explain why (a speed advantage)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Builders in Hong Kong have relied on bamboo scaffolding for generations.
• Workers fasten bamboo poles together with nylon strips, constructing frames that can envelop even skyscrapers.
• Bamboo is lightweight, so workers can carry the poles up by hand and assemble or dismantle a frame rapidly.
• The poles are also flexible, allowing a frame to conform to buildings with irregular shapes.
items.stem: The student wants to explain why bamboo scaffolding can be assembled quickly. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because bamboo poles are flexible, a scaffolding frame made from them can be shaped to fit around buildings that have unusual outlines.
Bamboo scaffolds, which can surround even skyscrapers, can be assembled and dismantled rapidly.
Since bamboo is light enough for workers to carry the poles up by hand, a bamboo scaffold can be assembled quickly.
In Hong Kong, workers fasten bamboo poles together with nylon strips to construct scaffolding frames around buildings.
items.explanation: The goal is to explain why bamboo scaffolding goes up quickly. Choice C gives the reason: bamboo is light, so workers can carry the poles up by hand.

A.why_wrong: It explains why bamboo frames can fit unusual buildings, not why they go up quickly.

B.why_wrong: It says the scaffolds can be put up quickly but does not explain why.

D.why_wrong: It describes how the frames are tied together but gives no reason they can be put up quickly.

items.notes: Subject: history and society (building trades). General knowledge, no named people. Distractors OG (another advantage with its own reason), PART (claim without reason, as in 2.15 B), OG.

fixes: cut bullet 5 (training), which no option used; 86 to 77 words

items.subtype: Explain the cause of a color
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lake Retba, a shallow lake near Senegal’s Atlantic coast, is known as Lac Rose because its water is distinctly pink.
• Its water is considerably saltier than seawater, and few organisms can tolerate it.
• One organism that flourishes there is Dunaliella salina, a microscopic alga.
• To shield itself from intense sunlight, the alga produces abundant quantities of a reddish pigment.
• Local workers harvest salt from the lakebed and sell it throughout the region.
items.stem: The student wants to explain why Lake Retba’s water is pink. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Because its water is considerably saltier than seawater, few organisms can tolerate conditions in Lake Retba.
Lake Retba’s water is pink because the salty lake is home to a microscopic alga that makes a red pigment to protect itself from the sun.
Lake Retba, a pink lake near Senegal’s Atlantic coast, is a source of salt that local workers harvest from its bed.
Dunaliella salina, a microscopic alga, produces abundant quantities of a reddish pigment to shield itself from intense sunlight.
items.explanation: Choice B explains the lake’s color: an alga that thrives in the salty water makes large amounts of red pigment, which turns the water pink.

A.why_wrong: It explains why few organisms live in the lake, not why the water is pink.

C.why_wrong: It mentions that the lake is pink but gives no cause for the color.

D.recipe: PART (the cause without the link to the lake)
D.why_wrong: It describes the alga’s pigment but never connects it to the lake or its color.

items.notes: Subject: science (microbiology). General knowledge. The notes state the color and the alga’s pigment in separate bullets and never connect them, so the key must make the link; D holds the cause but not the link (the 1.6 C pattern).

items.subtype: Similarity of two animals (a shared method)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The thorny devil is a spiny lizard inhabiting central Australia.
• It absorbs moisture from damp sand into tiny grooves between its scales, which channel the water to its mouth.
• The Texas horned lizard inhabits the southern United States and northern Mexico.
• During rainstorms, it collects water in tiny grooves between its scales, which channel the water to its mouth.
• When threatened, it can deter predators by squirting blood from its eyes.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the thorny devil and the Texas horned lizard. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Both the thorny devil and the Texas horned lizard drink using tiny grooves between their scales that move water to their mouths.
The thorny devil absorbs moisture from damp sand, whereas the Texas horned lizard collects rainwater during storms.
The Texas horned lizard, which inhabits the southern United States and northern Mexico, collects rainwater in grooves between its scales.
When threatened, the Texas horned lizard can deter predators by squirting blood from its eyes.
items.explanation: The notes describe each lizard drinking through tiny grooves between its scales that channel water to its mouth. Choice A emphasizes this similarity with “both.”

B.why_wrong: It contrasts where each lizard gets its water instead of stating what they share.

C.why_wrong: It describes only the Texas horned lizard.

D.why_wrong: It describes how one lizard defends itself and says nothing about the thorny devil.

items.notes: Subject: science (zoology). Moloch horridus and Phrynosoma cornutum both move water to the mouth through channels between the scales; general knowledge. Only one shared trait in the notes (habitats are given without a shared descriptor), so B is the lone REL option.

items.subtype: Relative degree (hardness)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The name “jade” is applied to two distinct minerals: nephrite and jadeite.
• Nephrite has been carved by artisans in China for thousands of years.
• Its hardness measures 6 to 6.5 on the Mohs scale, which ranks minerals by their resistance to scratching.
• Jadeite, considerably rarer, was especially prized by the Olmec and Maya civilizations of Mesoamerica.
• Its hardness measures 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize how the hardness of jadeite compares with that of nephrite. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: On the Mohs scale, nephrite’s hardness measures 6 to 6.5, and jadeite’s measures 6.5 to 7.
Nephrite and jadeite are two distinct minerals, but both are known as jade.
On the Mohs scale, jadeite ranks slightly higher in hardness than nephrite does.
Jadeite, which was especially prized by the Olmec and Maya, is the rarer of the two minerals called jade.
items.explanation: The goal is to compare the two minerals’ hardness. Jadeite ranks 6.5 to 7 on the Mohs scale and nephrite 6 to 6.5, so jadeite is slightly harder. Choice C states that comparison directly, without the raw numbers.

A.why_wrong: It gives both hardness values but never says which mineral is harder, so it does not emphasize the comparison.

B.why_wrong: It explains that both minerals are called jade, not how their hardness compares.

D.recipe: REL (comparison on the wrong measure: rarity)
D.why_wrong: It compares how rare the minerals are, not how hard they are.

items.notes: Subject: science (geology and gemology). Mohs values are standard. Key derives “slightly harder than” and drops the raw numbers, as in 2.44 C. Distractors LIST, OG, REL (wrong dimension, as in 2.44 D).

items.subtype: Explanation and example of a term
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• An endonym is the name that a group of people uses for itself, its language, or its homeland.
• An exonym is a name for a group or place that is used primarily by outsiders.
• Exonyms frequently arise when speakers of one language borrow and adapt a name from a neighboring language.
• The inhabitants of Germany refer to their country as Deutschland.
• In Finnish, Germany is called Saksa, a name derived from that of an ancient people, the Saxons.
items.stem: The student wants to provide an explanation and an example of an endonym. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: An endonym is the name a group uses for itself, its language, or its homeland, unlike an exonym, which is used by outsiders.
Saksa, the Finnish name for Germany, is an exonym, a name used primarily by outsiders for a group or place.
The inhabitants of Germany refer to their country as Deutschland, while speakers of Finnish call it Saksa.
An endonym is a name people use for their own group or place, such as Deutschland, which is what Germans call Germany.
items.explanation: The goal has two parts: explain what an endonym is and give an example. Choice D does both: it defines an endonym as a name people use for their own group or place and offers Deutschland, the Germans’ own name for their country.

A.why_wrong: It explains what an endonym is but gives no example.

B.recipe: OG (explains and illustrates the other term)
B.why_wrong: It explains and gives an example of an exonym, not an endonym.

C.why_wrong: It gives two names for Germany but never explains what an endonym is.

items.notes: Subject: social science (linguistics, place names). General knowledge. Distractors PART (definition only), OG (the neighboring term, explained and illustrated), PART (instances only), as in 2.16 and 1.19. The notes never label Deutschland an endonym, so the key makes that link.

items.subtype: Present a study’s findings (two findings merged)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many vineyards mow the vegetation between rows of grapevines to reduce competition for water.
• A team of researchers in Uruguay investigated whether grazing sheep could replace mechanical mowing.
• Over three growing seasons, they allowed sheep to graze half of a vineyard’s rows and mowed the remainder.
• Vegetation in the grazed rows remained approximately as short as vegetation in the mowed rows.
• Grape yields from vines in the two sets of rows were statistically indistinguishable.
items.stem: The student wants to present the study’s findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The researchers investigated whether sheep grazing in a vineyard could replace mechanical mowing of the vegetation between rows of grapevines.
In the study, sheep kept the plants between rows of vines about as short as mowing did, and grape harvests were about the same in grazed and mowed rows.
Over three growing seasons, the researchers allowed sheep to graze half of a vineyard’s rows while mowing the remainder.
Grape yields from vines in grazed rows and vines in mowed rows were statistically indistinguishable.
items.explanation: The study had two findings: vegetation in grazed rows stayed about as short as in mowed rows, and grape yields did not differ between the two sets of rows. Choice B presents both findings.

A.recipe: OG (the aim offered for the findings)
A.why_wrong: It states what the researchers wanted to learn, not what they found.

C.recipe: OG (the method offered for the findings)
C.why_wrong: It describes how the study was carried out, not its results.

D.why_wrong: It gives only the finding about grape yields and leaves out the finding about the vegetation between the rows.

items.notes: Subject: science (agriculture). Invented study, team unnamed (“a team of researchers in Uruguay”); the practice itself is real. Slot-swap distractors (aim, method) plus one partial finding, as in 2.5 and 3.10.

items.subtype: Describe an example to an audience familiar with its type
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A hórreo is a granary elevated on stone pillars, traditionally built in northwestern Spain to keep harvested grain dry and inaccessible to rodents.
• Flat slabs atop the pillars prevent rats from climbing into the storage chamber.
• The hórreo of Carnota, in Galicia, was completed in the late eighteenth century.
• Constructed of granite, it measures approximately 35 meters in length.
• It rests on 22 pairs of pillars, making it one of the longest hórreos in the region.
items.stem: The student wants to describe the hórreo of Carnota to an audience already familiar with hórreos. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Built of granite in the late 1700s, the hórreo of Carnota is about 35 meters long and stands on 22 pairs of pillars.
The hórreo of Carnota, in Galicia, is a granary elevated on stone pillars to keep harvested grain dry and inaccessible to rodents.
Like other hórreos, the hórreo of Carnota has flat slabs atop its pillars that prevent rats from climbing into its storage chamber.
Hórreos, which are granaries elevated on stone pillars, were traditionally built in northwestern Spain to keep harvested grain dry.
items.explanation: An audience that already knows what a hórreo is needs only the details of this one. Choice A gives them without explaining hórreos: the hórreo of Carnota is made of granite, dates from the late eighteenth century, is about 35 meters long, and stands on 22 pairs of pillars.

B.why_wrong: It explains what a hórreo is and does, which this audience already knows, and gives none of the features of the hórreo of Carnota.

C.recipe: AUD (a feature shared by all hórreos)
C.why_wrong: It describes the slabs that keep rats out of every hórreo, which this audience already knows, rather than what sets the hórreo of Carnota apart.

D.recipe: AUD + OG (the type, not the example)
D.why_wrong: It explains hórreos in general and does not describe the hórreo of Carnota at all.

items.notes: Subject: history and architecture (vernacular buildings). The Carnota hórreo (Galicia, about 35 m, 22 pairs of feet, granite, late eighteenth century) is general knowledge. Three AUD-type distractors, as in 2.18, where all three wrong options explain leporellos.

items.subtype: Specify a quantity (a depth)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Snailfish are a family of fish inhabiting environments from shallow coastal waters to the deepest oceanic trenches.
• In 2022, a research team lowered cameras into the Izu-Ogasawara Trench, south of Japan.
• The cameras recorded a juvenile snailfish swimming at a depth of 8,336 meters.
• Some scientists have predicted that fish cannot survive deeper than approximately 8,400 meters.
items.stem: The student wants to specify the depth at which the juvenile snailfish was filmed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Snailfish inhabit a wide range of environments, from shallow coastal waters to the deepest oceanic trenches.
Some scientists have predicted that fish cannot survive deeper than approximately 8,400 meters below the ocean’s surface.
The juvenile snailfish filmed in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench in 2022 was swimming 8,336 meters below the surface.
In 2022, a research team lowered cameras into the Izu-Ogasawara Trench, a deep ocean trench south of Japan.
items.explanation: Choice C gives the depth at which the snailfish was filmed: 8,336 meters below the surface.

A.why_wrong: It describes the range of depths where snailfish live, not the depth at which this one was filmed.

B.why_wrong: It gives the depth some scientists think fish cannot go beyond, not the depth where the snailfish was filmed.

D.recipe: OG (place and date of the study)
D.why_wrong: It says where and when the cameras were used but gives no depth.

items.notes: Subject: science (marine biology). The 2022 Izu-Ogasawara snailfish film (8,336 m) was widely reported; team left unnamed. B offers a second depth figure as the trap, as 2.39 C and D offer the other fruit’s data.

fixes: cut bullet 4 (record claim), which no option used; 83 to 73 words

items.subtype: Use a quotation to explain a choice
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Inés Guamán is a ceramicist from Chimborazo Province, in the Ecuadorian Andes.
• She shapes her vessels entirely by hand, rejecting the potter’s wheel as “too fast for the clay I know.”
• Rather than using a kiln, she fires her pottery in an open pit covered with dried vegetation and dung.
• The smoke leaves unpredictable black and gray markings on the clay’s surface.
• “I fire in the open so the fire can finish what my hands begin,” Guamán has explained.
items.stem: The student wants to use a quotation from Guamán to explain why she fires her pots in an open pit. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Guamán fires her pottery in an open pit, where the smoke leaves unpredictable black and gray markings on the clay’s surface.
Guamán fires her pots in an open pit rather than a kiln so that, in her words, “the fire can finish what my hands begin.”
Guamán, who shapes her vessels entirely by hand, has rejected the potter’s wheel as “too fast for the clay I know.”
Rather than using a kiln, Guamán fires her pottery in an open pit covered with dried vegetation and dung.
items.explanation: The goal calls for a quotation that explains why Guamán fires her pots in the open. Choice B quotes her reason: she fires in the open so that “the fire can finish what my hands begin.”

A.recipe: NOQ (paraphrase of an effect, no quotation)
A.why_wrong: It describes what the smoke does to the clay but includes no quotation from Guamán and does not give her reason.

C.recipe: NOQ (a quotation that explains another choice)
C.why_wrong: It quotes Guamán, but the quotation explains why she avoids the potter’s wheel, not why she fires in an open pit.

D.why_wrong: It describes how Guamán fires her pots but includes no quotation and no reason.

items.notes: Subject: arts (ceramics). Invented artist and quotations: “Inés Guamán” searched once (2026-10-16), no ceramicist or artist with that name found. Two quotations in the notes, as in 2.29, so one distractor quotes her for another purpose.

items.subtype: Specify a location
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ganvié is a village of approximately 20,000 inhabitants whose houses stand on stilts above the water.
• It is situated on Lake Nokoué, in southern Benin.
• Its founders settled on the lake centuries ago to escape slave raids on the mainland.
• Residents travel between homes, markets, and schools in wooden canoes.
• Many households depend on fishing for their income.
items.stem: The student wants to specify where Ganvié is located. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ganvié is a village of approximately 20,000 inhabitants who travel in wooden canoes.
The founders of Ganvié settled there centuries ago to escape slave raids on the mainland.
Many households in Ganvié, a village of houses built on stilts, depend on fishing for their income.
Ganvié, a village of houses built on stilts, is situated on Lake Nokoué in southern Benin.
items.explanation: Choice D specifies where Ganvié is: on Lake Nokoué, in southern Benin.

A.why_wrong: It gives the village’s population and how residents travel, not its location.

B.why_wrong: It explains why the village was founded but does not say where it is.

C.why_wrong: It describes residents’ work, not the village’s location.

items.notes: Subject: social science and history (settlement). General knowledge, no named people. Three OG distractors from the unused bullets, as in 1.9.

items.subtype: Emphasize a quantity
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Capiz is a mollusk found in the coastal waters of the Philippines.
• Its thin, translucent shells were traditionally used instead of glass in the windows of Filipino houses.
• Filipino artist Paolo Macatangay creates large-scale installations from capiz shells.
• His installation Tide Lines (2019) incorporates 12,000 shells strung on wire.
• The suspended strands collectively form the shape of a wave.
items.stem: The student wants to emphasize how many shells Macatangay used in Tide Lines. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Capiz shells, which are thin and translucent, were traditionally used instead of glass in Filipino windows.
In Tide Lines, suspended strands of capiz shells collectively form the shape of a wave.
To create Tide Lines, Macatangay strung together a total of 12,000 capiz shells.
Paolo Macatangay is a Filipino artist who creates large-scale installations from capiz shells.
items.explanation: Choice C emphasizes the number of shells by stating that Macatangay used a total of 12,000 of them in Tide Lines.

A.why_wrong: It describes how capiz shells were once used, not how many shells the work contains.

B.why_wrong: It describes the shape the shells form but not how many there are.

D.why_wrong: It introduces the artist but says nothing about the number of shells in Tide Lines.

items.notes: Subject: arts (installation). Invented artist and work. The writer’s “Paolo Manalastas” shared a surname with a real Filipino artist, Diana Grace Manalastas, so the reviewer renamed him “Paolo Macatangay” (Macatangay is a Batangas surname); searched 2026-10-16: no artist of that name, and no capiz or installation artist named Macatangay. Key adds the emphatic frame “a total of,” as in 1.15.

fixes: renamed the invented artist Paolo Manalastas to Paolo Macatangay (a real Filipino artist, Diana Grace Manalastas, shares the old surname); searched once, no artist of that name

items.subtype: Describe a form (a symbol)
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Adinkra are visual symbols originally created by the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.
• Each symbol represents a proverb or a philosophical idea.
• Sankofa is among the most widely recognized adinkra symbols.
• A common version depicts a bird whose feet face forward while its head is turned backward.
• The bird carries an egg in its beak.
items.stem: The student wants to describe what the Sankofa symbol commonly shows. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Sankofa is among the most widely recognized symbols created by the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.
A common version of Sankofa shows a bird looking back over its body, with its feet pointing forward and an egg held in its beak.
Adinkra symbols, such as Sankofa, were originally created by the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.
Like the other adinkra symbols, Sankofa represents a proverb or a philosophical idea.
items.explanation: Choice B describes what the symbol shows: a bird with its feet facing forward and its head turned back, holding an egg in its beak.

A.why_wrong: It says the symbol is well known and who created it, not what it shows.

C.why_wrong: It identifies the people who created adinkra symbols but does not describe Sankofa.

D.why_wrong: It says Sankofa stands for an idea, not what the symbol looks like.

items.notes: Subject: arts and culture (visual symbols). General knowledge; the bird is one common form of Sankofa (another is a stylized heart), so the notes say “a common form.” Three OG distractors, as in 1.1.

items.subtype: Explain the origin of a name
items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Canary Islands are a Spanish archipelago off the northwest coast of Africa.
• The islands take their name from Canaria, the name the ancient Romans used for one of them.
• According to the Roman writer Pliny the Elder, that island was named for the enormous dogs found there.
• The canary, a small songbird native to the islands, was subsequently named after them.
items.stem: The student wants to explain the origin of the Canary Islands’ name. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Canary Islands are named after Canaria, an island that Pliny the Elder said was named for its enormous dogs.
The canary, a small songbird native to the Canary Islands, was named after the islands.
The Canary Islands, which belong to Spain, form an archipelago off the northwest coast of Africa.
The Roman writer Pliny the Elder wrote about Canaria, one of the islands in the archipelago off the northwest coast of Africa.
items.explanation: Choice A explains where the islands’ name came from: the Roman name Canaria, which Pliny the Elder reported was given to that island because of its enormous dogs.

B.recipe: OG (explains the bird’s name, not the islands’)
B.why_wrong: It explains how the canary got its name, not how the islands got theirs.

C.why_wrong: It says where the islands are, not where their name comes from.

D.why_wrong: It mentions Pliny the Elder but does not say what he reported about the name.

items.notes: Subject: history (place names). Pliny the Elder’s account (Natural History, book 6) that Canaria was named for its many large dogs is standard; the bird takes its name from the islands. B is the tempting reversal of a common belief, but true and off-goal.

fixes: cut bullet 4 (Latin canis), which no option used; 85 to 78 words
